title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Energy Sector Development Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative:
Scope: The tranche 1 ($164 million) of Energy MFF comprises of following sub-projects:
(i) NEPS 220 kV transmission line (Kunduz - Taluqan) -- $27.8 million - construction of a 67km double circuit 220kv transmission line linking cities of Taluqan to Kunduz. (ii) NEPS distribution network in Kunduz and Baghlan -- $51.3 million - development and rehabilitation of 20kv and low voltage networks for 45,000 households in Kunduz and Baghlan cities (iii) Rehabilitation of Sheberghan gas wells in 2 phases -- $21.8 million - rehabilitation of dilapidated gas wells in Shiberghan to enable extraction of domestic gas to power future gas fired power generation in Jawzjan province. (iv) NEPS 220kv system operation and maintenance (O&M) emergency equipment -- $19.0 million - Consulting services to assist the operation and maintenance of the newly constructed 220kv NEPS. Procurement under process. (v) Project management and implementation for tranche I & II -- $23.0 million - Consulting services to assist the management of projects in DABS. (vi) Future sub-projects' preparation -- $5.3 million (vii) Individual consultants -- $0.5 million (viii) Implementation supervision Gas wells rehabilitation and capacity building of Ministry of Mines -- $1.2 million - design and supervision consultancy

Output: Rehabilitation of 8-12 gas wells in Sheberghan Indicator: Gas Wells Rehabilitation and flow production increased to 900,000 cubic meters per day by 2015 (based line: 350000 cubic meters per day in 2010). Progress/Status: Sheberghan Gas Wells Rehabilitation project is consists of the rehabilitation of 8 - 12 gas wells in Sheberghan in northern Afghanistan. Phase 1 of the gas wells rehabilitation for eight gas wells (Well No. 21, 29, 32, 38, 45, 47, 61, and 69) was awarded to the Turkish Petroleum Corporation in August 2012. Out of eight wells, six gas wells (Well No. 21, 38, 45, 47, 61, and 69) were successfully rehabilitated and two gas wells (Well No. 29 and 32) were failed due to the technical issue of tubing corrosion and excessive water flow amount. The optimal flow rate of six rehabilitated wells was about 1.32 million cubic meters of the gas/day for use by the industrial, commercial, and residential customers. The project was completed in October 2014.
Phase 2, of gas wells rehabilitation for two existing gas wells in Yatimtaq Gas Field of Sherberghan, was awarded to Xinjing Zhengtong Oil and Gas Co. Ltd in August 2016. The contractor mobilized at the construction site in February 2018. The contractor drilled well No.31 and 37 up to the depth 1,600 meters (m) (targeted depth), meanwhile, the contractor explores different options to supply radioactive and explosive materials for logging and perforation of both wells. Wells number 31 and 37 completed and MoMP provided the completion certificate on 21 August 2018. The optimal flow rate of two rehabilitated wells is 166,032 million cubic meters of the gas/day. The project extension was approved from 1 July 2018 to 31 August 2018 so the remaining works can be completed. The project was completed on 21 August 2018. Due to the long delay in the procurement process, and MoMP's request, the project for the supervision consultant package ($1m) was canceled. MoMP has committed to take over the project supervision and oversight with its own resource using Afghan Gas Enterprise staff. Data Source: ICE quarterly report CSO publications MoMP Project Progress Report Actual value:

Output: Stabilization of NEPS operations and maintenance (O&M) system instituted for efficient functioning of grid. Indicator: NEPS system losses reduced from 50% in 2007 to 30% 2017 Progress/Status: The contracts for Lot 1 & 3 were awarded to Netrocon Consortium and Unit Export Limited in May 2014 after two rounds of bidding for the supply of emergency equipment of Operations and Maintenance (O&M) for 220-kV NEPS transmission lines ($14.26 million). The supply of equipment under Lot 1 and Lot 3 was 100% completed on 16 Dec 2016.
Lot 2 was advertised twice but failed to solicit technical bidders, thus the EA requested the cancellation of Lot 2 ($0.3 million) due to a low amount and dismal response. Data Source: ICE quarterly report DABS annual report Consumer surveys Project Progress Reports

Output: Evacuation of power in NEPS area through Kunduz Taloqan transmission line Indicator: Installation of 220-kV, 70 kms transmission line from Kunduz to Taloqan by 2015. baseline: nil) Progress/Status: The contract for 65.5 km of the double circuit, 220-kV Kunduz-Taluqan Transmission Line was awarded to the KEC-Netracon consortium on 18 December 2011. The project is located partially in Kunduz and Takhar province connecting both provinces in the northern part of Afghanistan. The total contract amount was $27.8 million and the amount financed by ADB is about 26.0 million and disbursed. The project was completed on 11 November 2013. Power system capable to supply 1,450 megawatts (MW) of connected load by 2017 from North East Power System (NEPS) from 400MW in 2010 Progress/Status: The power system is capable to supply 450 megawatts (MW) of the connected load from North East Power System (NEPS) (150 MW from Tajikistan and 300 MW from Uzbekistan). Various donors along with ADB are implementing respective programs to extend NEPS' capacity and strengthen institutional arrangements for Operations and Management (O&M) of power infrastructure in Afghanistan. The physical work of 600 km of 500 kV power transmission line connecting TKM grid to AFG is under construction starting from TKM border till Kabul and associated substations with expected completion by 2021. The proposed 500 kV line will increase the supply up to 1,300 MW upon completion. Data Source: ICE quarterly report Da Afghanistan Beshna Sherkat (DABS) annual report Consumer surveys Actual value:
